source.title: Interactive machine vision for wildlife conservation

record.file_problem: None; the full thesis text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The thesis discusses weakly supervised wildlife detection, but does not test or rely on the claim that a strong model fine-tuned on a weaker model’s labels can outperform that supervisor. Its weak labels are image-level presence/count annotations, not labels generated by a weaker model.
record.gate_note: Chapter 4 reports results for weakly supervised object detection with image-level labels and a small amount of positional ground truth. This is a related but different supervision setup, so those results are recorded under fits_no_version, not as tests of V1–V6. Cited results and general background are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The thesis neither tests nor uses weak-to-strong generalization. Its 'weak supervision' means human-provided image-level presence/absence or count labels for a CNN detector (Chapter 4). It is not labels generated by a weaker model for a stronger student. No PGR, weak supervisor or strong ceiling in the claim's sense appears anywhere. The original paper (2023) postdates this 2020 thesis and is not cited. 'cites_only' is the closest enum, but strictly the thesis neither cites nor discusses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The thesis concludes that interactive machine vision (CNN training practices, Transfer Sampling active learning, weak supervision with few positional labels, the AIDE platform) greatly reduces wildlife-census annotation effort. It draws no conclusion about weak-to-strong generalization.
record.recipe_differences: No weak-to-strong training recipe is tested. Chapter 4 uses human-provided image-level presence/count labels and a small fraction of human positional annotations.
record.method_sensitivity: In the adjacent weak-supervision experiments, detection results depend on the supervision type and positional distance threshold; the counts-only model is described as performing well at 40 pixels but not at 30 pixels.

fits_no_version.finding: A density-map CNN trained on human image-level counts, plus positional labels for 1% of images (3 images), performs on par with a fully position-supervised model on Kuzikus UAV wildlife detection. Binary-only supervision lags behind the other models. Count MAE is 0.79 for both count models versus 1.28 for full dense (Table 4.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weakly supervised (image-level human label) object detection with sparse full supervision can match full supervision in aerial wildlife detection.

record.problems: The weak-supervision results do not address the specified weak-model-to-strong-model claim. The Chapter 4 detection comparisons are described qualitatively in text and precision-recall plots; uncertainty estimates for those results are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No results relevant to the six claim versions were omitted. General results from Chapters 2, 3, and 5, and cited prior-work results, were not extracted because they do not test the claim or add relevant weak-to-strong evidence.

untested.parts: No weaker model generates labels; no PGR.
No confidence loss, supervisor ensembling or loss variants for weak-to-strong training.
No variation of supervisor or student size, and no PGR predictors.
No weak-to-strong failure modes; domain shift in Chapter 3 is an unrelated active-learning adaptation.
Vision experiments exist, but none uses weak-model supervision of a stronger model.

missing.what: Table 4.2 count MAE/MSE per supervision variant (e.g. Binary 1.96/22.29; Counts+1% 0.79/1.59; Full dense 1.28/2.75). Relevant only to the fits_no_version finding, not to any version.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'discusses' relation overstates the link: the thesis never mentions weak-to-strong generalization. 'Weak supervision' here is the WSOD sense (cheaper human labels), a terminological false match. Row states should be cannot_determine, since no version applies.

versions.untested_parts: No weaker model labels a dataset for a stronger model; no weak-supervisor comparison or PGR.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensemble, or loss-variant comparison for weak-to-strong training.
No weak-to-strong PGR analysis across model sizes, tasks, or representations.
No weak-to-strong failure-mode analysis of supervisor limitations, distribution shift, or shared errors.
No theory of when a student must outperform a weaker supervisor.
No weak-to-strong test in vision; the vision experiments use human-provided image-level or positional labels, not labels from a weaker model.
